verdict.rationale: cubic's review automations (review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, custom agents) are defined in a repository-resident `cubic.yaml` that is the documented source of truth. That puts automation config under the repo's version history and PR review, but cubic itself documents no versioning, change review, or rollback for these automations. Auto-approval's shadow mode is a dry-run preview before going live, not versioning or rollback. Missing for 10: first-party docs on automation version history, a review/approval flow for config changes, an explicit rollback mechanism, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: `cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Create a repository named `cubic-config` in your organization and add a `cubic.yaml` file to the root directory.
Start in shadow mode to see which PRs cubic would approve, then switch to live mode
